# C14 — API Client projects and document lifecycle

Phase: P04. Status: planned. Required predecessor: C13.

## Outcome

Rebuild local-first workbench authoring without GPUI coupling.

## Inputs and dependency gates

C13; approved request-document/storage contracts and reviewed importer formats.

Read the [common execution contract](../IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md),
[review protocol](../review-protocol.md), and [test catalogue](../test-catalogue.md).
Concrete interfaces follow accepted G01 ADRs. Read the [selected design](../../architecture/DESIGN.md),
[qualification contract](../../architecture/qualification.md) and this chunk's
exact target in [checks.json](../../architecture/checks.json). Freeze all source/shared dependency
inputs; active neighboring worktrees and unavailable methods cannot count as pins.

## Milestones

1. Implement collections/tabs/edit/save/conflicts/drafts, environments/variables/secret references, schemas and imports.
2. Preserve fresh-input/revision reconciliation when saving or replacing a document during typing or invalid input.
3. Implement Git view/profile adoption and built-in SCM collection as generic request specifications, not proof of dedicated workflows.
4. Keep managed AIRS credentials separate from arbitrary workbench targets; treat imports as data, never executable code.

## Required acceptance

- Production React Save tests cover click-before-debounce, invalid input and faithful revision/conflict behavior.

- Any changed UI also requires T09 actual native keyboard/focus/accessibility checks; global requirements are not deferred solely to C24.

- T06,T14,T18: save while typing, invalid edit, stale saved baseline, interrupted durable write, conflict and close guard.
- Bounded cURL/Insomnia/schema/profile imports reject malformed/traversal inputs and leave sources unchanged.
- Native local-first authoring/restart/secret-reference/import/keyboard flows; inspect current shipping API Client feature coverage.

G01/C01 must bind these assertions to exact commands and fixture/native targets
before execution. Run appropriate regressions when changes reach earlier chunks.
No test result, native acceptance, or live qualification is claimed by this file.

## Evidence and completion

T23 is mandatory here for this feature's local work and reconnect behavior: offline launch/read/edit, explicit retry, preserved uncertain outcomes, and no replay of pending reviews/scans/inference/HTTP mutations/tool calls. C24 repeats the cumulative matrix.

Workbench workflow matrix, persistence/import contracts, document-authority causal probes and native authoring evidence.

Use the [implementer prompt](../prompts/implement-chunk.md) and
[independent reviewer prompt](../prompts/review-chunk.md). Require ≥9/10 overall
and in architecture, behavior, authority/security, and validation; no required
fixes or absent mandatory evidence. Preserve attempts, raw verdicts, hashes, and
remediation. Commit only the reviewed tree; do not unlock the next chunk early.

## Safety and recovery

Synthetic projects only. No network execution yet; preserve source profiles and recover destination drafts on rollback.
# C14 follow-ups for the P04 push to 9/10 (D034)

C14 completed at 8/10 under D034 (8d219b0). Codex attempt-02 scored
9/8/9/9/8 with no blockers, after attempt-01's R1–R5 and E1 were remediated
(`remediation-attempt-01.md`). The remaining findings are remediated in the
tree re-reviewed as C14 at the P04 push; D040 and DESIGN.md's save row
record the rule.

- R5 (remaining, medium), body ownership by the file reached:
  - `document::shared` no longer compares the literal reference. A body is
    written only when the file it reaches is owned by no one else: not
    another request file's body (duplicates and invalid ones included),
    and not a project file (any request file, this one included,
    `collection.toml`, an environment, a schema).
  - Names are compared by the file itself (device and inode of the
    resolved path) or, for a file not yet written, by the case-folded
    name. Case and Unicode-normalization aliases on the Mac's volumes are
    therefore refused as `sharedBody`.
  - Tests:
    - The production-interface
      `a_body_is_owned_by_the_file_it_reaches_not_its_spelling` runs on the
      case- and normalization-insensitive temporary volume. A different
      case, a decomposed Unicode spelling, another request's metadata file
      and `collection.toml` each return `sharedBody` with every project
      byte unchanged, and an independent body still saves.
    - The unit test
      `a_body_not_yet_written_is_owned_by_its_case_folded_name` covers a
      missing file reserved by an invalid request.
- Suggestion, leaving a document: the React test is now "protects pending
  edits when leaving the document, before the pause would". It requires the
  Protect within a quarter of the typing pause after the editor leaves, so
  the pause's own timer cannot satisfy it; the "leaving a document drops
  pending edits" probe is caught.
- Probe, parent components: with `creating` set, the hidden-name rule
  refused `..` too, so removing both parent guards survived. The guarded
  test now also checks `..` and `.` with `creating` off (`../a`, `a/../b`,
  `a/..`, `./a`, `a/./b`), and the probe is caught.
- Probe anchors: "Save sends the loaded fields" names the Save snapshot
  uniquely (C15 added a Send snapshot). "Duplicate requests lose their body
  ownership" targets the new owner filter. Three probes cover identity,
  case and project-file aliases.

# Prisma AIRS Desktop v2 domain vocabulary

These terms name the desktop product and its native authority concepts.
Mechanisms, wire formats and transition rules belong in the selected design.

## Language

**Tenant profile**: An application-owned configuration for a Prisma AIRS tenant,
including its label, endpoints, and protected credential references. A scan-only
profile does not require management OAuth credentials. A profile is not an
Academy learner account or a Gateway workspace.

**Credential capability**: The specific operations a credential can authorize,
such as scanning, management, inference, or workspace MCP. Possessing one
capability does not establish another; configuration keeps them explicit.

**Gateway workspace**: A remote AI Gateway administrative/inference context within
the selected tenant profile. It is distinct from a local filesystem project.

**Configuration review**: An operator-visible proposal for an AIRS configuration
change, bound to the current tenant, credential context, target resource, and
draft. Rust owns its validity. Displaying or importing a proposal does not grant
permission to apply it.

**Remote outcome**: What is known about an attempted remote action: not sent,
rejected, completed as established by evidence, or unknown. Local timeout,
cancellation, and disconnection do not establish remote rollback.

**Academy feature**: The learner experience within the broader desktop app.
Presentation is shared with Academy; remote learning contracts remain hosted.
Learning progression, XP, cosmetic credits, awards, and other gamification stay
within this feature.

**Academy learner account**: The remote learning identity owning progress,
assessments, certificates, and account-scoped local drafts/downloads. It is
independent of the selected Prisma AIRS tenant and Harness inference sign-in.

**Shared presentation**: React controls, themes, and shell layout reused from the
Academy-owned source. Sharing appearance does not share learner authority,
gamification effects, manager routes, or browser-session assumptions globally.

**Harness**: The assistant feature using the native Rust agent engine and
desktop-owned lifecycle, credential grants, reviews, and protected history.
The SCM SDK is a separate dependency, not the Harness engine.

**Project scope**: The explicitly selected local filesystem scope and approved
tool permissions available to a Harness conversation. Preserve the existing
restrictions initially; a transcript is not permission to restore approvals.

**MCP grant**: A desktop-owned authorization context for a specific remote MCP
binding. Inference sign-in is separate. Discovery does not establish execution;
execution evidence must correspond to the actual approved call.

**Historical conversation**: Saved user work that can be inspected after import.
Resumption requires separate context/protocol compatibility validation. It never
restores pending approvals or old authentication sessions.

**Billing**: Desktop commercial charging/monetization machinery, excluded from
v2. Remote Gateway usage/cost/budget/limit administration remains product
functionality. Academy's earned learning economy remains Academy-local.

**Shipped backend runtime**: Executables/workers required by the installed app's
backend. Node/Bun and TypeScript backend workers are excluded. Build-time JS
tooling and React JavaScript executing in the WebView are separate concepts.

**Parity**: Coverage of agreed working v1 behavior with new v2 evidence. V1 source
implementation, retained fixture/contract results, retained live evidence, and
v2 installed-artifact results are distinct. Replacing a preview/stub with a live
feature is scope expansion, not implicit parity work.

**Authority principal**: The native-established operator or restricted Harness
identity on whose behalf desktop work is requested. A claimed identity in a
request is not an Authority principal.

**Authority handle**: A principal-scoped entry to native desktop operations and
observations. Possessing an operation reference does not expand its authority.

**Intent**: A typed request for a specific desktop action under the caller's
current authority. It is distinct from a Harness proposal or an arbitrary remote
request.

**Receipt**: Native acknowledgement that an Intent was admitted, with its request
or operation reference. It is not evidence of operator confirmation or remote
completion.

**Refusal**: Native rejection of an Intent before admission under the requested
authority. A remote action's failure is a Remote outcome instead.

**ViewScope**: The product context a caller asks to observe, such as a learner
account, tenant workspace or Harness conversation. Native authority determines
which part is visible to that caller.

**Observation**: A scoped redacted view of native desktop state and operation
progress. It confers no execution or credential authority.

**ContextRef**: A native reference to the particular product context presented
to the caller. Returning to the same tenant or account does not revive retired
authority.

**Delivery session**: The current native-registered channel for one caller's
Intent deliveries. It is separate from tenant, learner or inference identity.

**Delivery sequence**: The order identity of an Intent within its Delivery session,
used to distinguish duplicate delivery from an explicit new action.
_Avoid_: Business retry, authorization token

**Native-owned payload reference**: A scoped reference to staged desktop input
whose ownership and content are known natively. It is not permission to read an
arbitrary filesystem path.

**Reviewed**: A Configuration review whose captured proposal remains eligible for
operator confirmation.

**Confirming**: A Configuration review currently awaiting the native operator's
answer for that specific proposal.

**Consumed**: A Configuration review already committed to its single admitted
operation. Failure of that operation does not make the review reusable.

**Queued**: An admitted desktop operation whose remote dispatch has not been
claimed.

**DispatchClaimed**: A desktop operation for which remote dispatch may have begun.
Local cancellation at this stage does not prove NotSent.

**Settled**: A desktop operation with a recorded terminal local result and its
current Remote outcome. Later reconciliation may refine knowledge of that outcome.

**Harness grant**: Native authority for one verified inference identity and its
approved tenant/workspace/origin context. Rotating that identity's token material
is distinct from replacing or revoking the Harness grant.

**Grant epoch**: The particular lifetime of a native grant's authority. Retired
authority stays retired even when an equivalent identity is selected again.

**One-time secret receipt**: The operator-scoped acknowledgement holding newly
issued secret material for its explicit transient reveal. It is separate from a
stored credential lookup.

**Editor lease**: The hold on the reviewed document while native operator
confirmation is pending. A changed document or context invalidates that hold.
# Independent review and evidence protocol

Applies to G00/G01 as planning/design reviews, every implementation chunk and
every phase. Scope the verdict honestly: a plan review evaluates the plan and
future gates, not application code or tests that do not exist.

G00/G01 were reviewed by Claude Code; those records are historical and cover
only their recorded inputs. Under D026, Claude Code implements and Codex is the
independent reviewer for C01–C26 and the phase reviews P01–P08.

## Gate

Actual independent Codex review must score at least 9/10 overall and in each
critical dimension: architecture, behavior, authority_security, validation.
No blocking or required fixes may remain. Missing mandatory evidence, stale
inputs, or a mismatched receipt prevents completion independently of scores.

The implementer cannot substitute its own score or edit the reviewer's verdict.
Do not ask a reviewer to raise a score; fix findings and request a new review.
Retain all attempts and explain remediation. Optional suggestions may remain
only when explicitly classified as nonrequired and consistent with the plan.

## Dimensions

- **Architecture:** depth at domain interfaces; locality; justified seams/real
  adapters; authoritative ownership; no needless pass-through layers or hidden
  cross-module coupling. Use the glossary and accepted ADRs.
- **Behavior:** complete chunk requirements, exact working-v1 subset, correct
  success/denied/empty/stale/partial/unknown outcomes, and no invented support.
- **Authority/security:** context/credential isolation, review/approval binding,
  trusted hosted assessment, protected storage, safe external destinations,
  bounded execution, provenance, Node-free shipped backend, and secret hygiene.
- **Validation:** meaningful production-interface tests; independent external
  expectations; required native/live/artifact evidence; reproducibility, hashes,
  explicit limitations, and causal failure cases. Test counts alone earn no score.

Scores below 9 require concrete findings with locations, impact, and acceptance
conditions. Even a 9/10 verdict with a required fix cannot pass.

Owner rule D034 (2026-10-18): a chunk may complete on a review scoring at least
8 in every dimension with no blockers; its remaining findings are recorded as
accepted failures. The reviewer still scores against the 9/10 gate above. At
the end of each phase every chunk accepted below 9 is remediated and
re-reviewed until it passes the full gate, before the phase review.

## Phase reviews

After the last chunk of a phase completes, request a cumulative Codex review of
that phase (P01: C01–C03, P02: C04–C07, P03: C08–C12, P04: C13–C15, P05: C16–C18,
P06: C19–C22, P07: C23–C24, P08: C25–C26). The phase packet binds the current
committed tree, every chunk receipt in the phase and earlier phases' receipts,
the phase's integrated test/native results rerun against that tree, and the
diff since the previous phase. The reviewer assesses integration across the
phase and the earlier features it affects. The same five-score threshold and
empty required_fixes/blockers/evidence_gaps apply, with no owner acceptance
(D034), and every member chunk must hold a passing 9/10 completion. The next phase does not
begin until its predecessor phase review passes. Historical chunk scores are
inputs to assess, never a substitute.

## Review transport

The controller writes an immutable request packet (request/attempt IDs, chunk or
phase, scope, predecessor receipts, source/dependency/build-flag/evidence
fingerprints, exact commands/results/evidence paths, diff, limitations, the
verdict schema and one absolute verdict path), then delivers it:

- Preferred: the owner-designated Codex thread, addressed by exact ID through
  `codex queue --thread <id> --message <text>`; never `--last`. A prior
  reviewer-authored handshake file proves routing. Queue success is submission
  only. The controller waits with bounded progress for the matching verdict.
- Fallback: a fresh `codex exec --sandbox read-only --ignore-user-config
  --ignore-rules --ephemeral` reviewer with web search disabled, approval
  policy never, `--output-schema` and captured JSONL stdout/stderr. It is
  recorded as a fresh reviewer under a new attempt; the prior attempt is
  expired so a late verdict cannot advance the gate. No bypass flags.

The verdict must validate against the strict schema, echo the request ID and
supplied fingerprints, and the frozen inputs must be unchanged afterwards.

## Receipt fields

Record review ID, chunk/gate/phase ID, attempt, request ID, transport (thread
ID or fresh exec), time, actual harness/version/model when reported, input prompt hash, source fingerprint, dependency manifest hash,
check/evidence manifest hash, raw output hash, reviewer scores, findings,
required fixes, blocking findings, limitations, and whether source stayed frozen.
For final packages also bind pre-sign/post-sign/stapled artifact hashes and the
installed-byte inventory. A review of a different tree or package cannot pass.

The input fingerprint includes tracked/nonignored source, instruction files,
configuration, file modes/symlink targets, and exact compiled dependency inputs.
Document narrow exclusions for review outputs/mutable status to avoid circular
hashes. Exclusions cannot hide application sources, lockfiles, generated bindings,
build flags, fixture rules, tests, notices, or package inventories. Evidence and
status hashes remain independently recorded even when excluded from source hash.

Use actual Codex review. The fresh fallback runs read-only, ephemeral, without
user configuration/rules, web search, hooks or connectors; the controller verifies
the effective settings it can observe rather than assuming the sandbox disables
every tool. The preferred thread's own sandbox is not controlled by this project;
its read-only obligation is instructed and enforced by unchanged pre/post
fingerprints. The reviewer may write only its designated review artifacts.
The reviewer reads project guidance and the exact scoped files/evidence deliberately. Evidence hashes detect
stale/tampered records; they are not cryptographic proof of provider authorship.

## Completion and invalidation

All predecessors must have passing receipts. Checks must be executed against
the same inputs and exact intended feature/build flags. Record each result as
passed, failed, blocked, or not applicable with a reason. An unavailable required
check is blocked, never silently not applicable.

On a failed gate: keep chunk active, fix findings, rerun affected checks plus
any regression surface the fix reaches, freeze new inputs, and obtain a fresh
independent review. A dependency update reopens affected consumers. Final release
revalidates cumulative behavior and source-bound prior evidence; it cannot merely
sum historical 9s from incompatible versions.

Completion is followed by a focused commit whose tree is verified against the
reviewed source. Changes to source after review require a new relevant review.
Git publication uses normal pushes to the specified v2 remote; no force-push.

## Evidence handling

Repository summaries contain reproducible commands, environments, hashes,
nonsecret fixture IDs, pass/fail/blocked status, and limitations. Keep real
credentials, prompts/responses, tokens, Keychain exports, unredacted traces,
customer records, signing secrets, and signed-in browser captures private.
Redact output before publication; retain original sensitive evidence in private
operator storage with a hash reference when appropriate.

The C01 controller must reject a score8 in any dimension, required fixes despite
score9, missing check results, changed dependency/source hashes, edited raw output,
duplicate/invalid receipt IDs, changed build flags, malformed schemas, and missing
native/artifact proof. Completion state is not writable by a reviewer or inferred
from a successful CLI exit code or queue acknowledgement alone. It also rejects
a verdict whose request ID or echoed fingerprints differ from the packet, a
verdict for an expired attempt, and a phase completion lacking a passing phase
review.

# Prisma AIRS Desktop v2 implementation plan

Status: product interview decisions D001–D023 accepted; D024/D025 settle source
terms and all four architecture candidates; D026 makes Codex the independent
chunk and phase reviewer. G00/G01 passed; implementation proceeds from C01. A passing plan review is not a passing architecture,
SDK, application, live-tenant, or package review.

## Outcome and exclusions

Deliver a fresh macOS Apple Silicon desktop application with React presentation
in Tauri, a focused Rust application core, direct Rust SCM SDK integration, and
the native Rust Harness engine. Academy supplies shared presentation and remains
the authority for remote learning. Preserve agreed working v1 behavior, using
v1 as requirements reference. Do not translate its GPUI implementation wholesale.

No desktop billing, media-generation backend, local MySQL/Redis server stack,
Node/Bun backend runtime, TypeScript workers, speculative browser client, or
in-app updater is included. Academy gamification remains inside Academy. Gateway
usage/cost/budget/limits remain operational product functionality. Build-time
JavaScript tooling and React WebView JavaScript are expected.

Source destination: `ssh://git@git-ssh.cdot.io/cdot/prisma-airs-desktop-v2.git`.
Checkout: `/Users/cdot/development/redtail/prisma-airs-desktop-v2`.

## Architectural guiding principles

1. Design deep modules: substantial behavior behind a small domain interface.
   Apply the deletion test; do not wrap every SDK method in a pass-through module.
2. The interface is the test surface. Exercise production transitions and
   adapters; use independent wire/protocol expectations for external contracts.
3. One adapter is a hypothetical seam; two real adapters justify a seam. Shared
   Academy presentation has real web/desktop consumers. Do not build speculative
   browser/backend/plugin architectures for this desktop delivery.
4. Rust owns authority and locality for tenant/credential/workspace context,
   request lifecycle, configuration review, protected storage, and approvals.
   React owns presentation and editable input, not permission to execute.
5. The SDK owns its declared transport/authentication contracts. The application
   owns interactive identity, OS storage, context admission, and workflow policy.
   Do not duplicate SDK retry/pagination/OAuth policy without a documented need.
6. Unknown outcomes and partial/stale/denied/unsupported data remain distinct.
   Never map an unknown verdict to allow or a cancelled write to successful rollback.
7. Host credentials and capabilities are explicit. No ambient environment-file
   discovery, inherited production fallback, generic renderer secret access,
   unrestricted native plugin grants, or cross-origin credential forwarding.
8. Shared appearance does not imply shared learner state. Tenant operations,
   Academy identity/progression, Harness inference identity, and MCP grants stay
   separately scoped. A tenant switch does not sign the learner out of Academy.
9. Keep provenance and reproducibility local to dependency selection. Exact
   versions, source hashes, build inputs, notices, and protocol pins are evidence;
   a neighboring active worktree is not a release dependency.
10. Measure native usability/performance and the actual installed package. A
    successful browser render or mocked IPC assertion is insufficient evidence
    for Tauri host behavior, VoiceOver, Keychain, sidecar isolation, or notarization.

Concrete interfaces, crate decomposition, shared package extraction, and storage
formats are outputs of G01. This plan defines behavior and testable work, not
unreviewed Rust signatures or a predetermined hierarchy of tiny modules.

## Ordered phases and chunks

Every Cxx has its own instruction file under [chunks](chunks/README.md). Complete
chunks in numeric order. A dependency delay blocks its chunk; report it honestly
and continue only research/preparation explicitly within that chunk. Do not
silently advance a later phase or replace a real dependency with a fake to pass.
For a prolonged upstream stall, report the exact dependency and offer an owner
reorder/scope decision. Do not wait indefinitely or reorder silently; an approved
change updates predecessors, plan and review evidence before execution.

| Phase | Chunks   | Result                                                           |
|-------|----------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| P00   | G00, G01 | Confirmed plan; selected and reviewed architecture               |
| P01   | C01–C03  | Shared desktop shell, native core, first complete Runtime scan   |
| P02   | C04–C07  | Academy identity, learner presentation, assessment, offline work |
| P03   | C08–C12  | Runtime/DLP administration, Sessions, reports, Library           |
| P04   | C13–C15  | Existing Red Team/Model reads and complete API Client workflows  |
| P05   | C16–C18  | Gateway workspace/configuration, reviewed changes, inference     |
| P06   | C19–C22  | Native Harness, Rust sign-in, typed host tools, workspace MCP    |
| P07   | C23–C24  | Reviewed imports, native quality, accessibility/privacy closure  |
| P08   | C25–C26  | Controlled live qualification; signed installed DMG acceptance   |

### G00 — Plan confirmation

Finish the decision ledger, baseline coverage, chunk instructions, review/test
protocols, dependency gates, and architecture handoff. Obtain an actual independent
plan review meeting D019. Product decisions are accepted and the owner explicitly
selected the architecture candidates and source terms in D024/D025. Continue the
requested design work; no further blanket scope question is needed. Architecture
review and implementation evidence remain distinct gates.

### G01 — Architecture improvement workflow

Follow [the handoff](architecture-handoff.md) and the requested
improve-codebase-architecture skill. Explore the named areas, show a temporary
HTML report with before/after candidates, ask the owner to choose, and grill the
selected design. Produce ADRs, interface/test ownership, dependency/import
decisions, and concrete chunk command specifications. Review the architecture
at least 9/10 in every critical dimension and overall. Revise this plan if the
selected design affects it, then re-review affected planning evidence.

No application scaffolding, shared-source refactoring, real-data migration,
product endpoint calls, or packaging implementation begins before G01 passes.

## Per-chunk execution contract

1. Read AGENTS/CLAUDE, glossary, accepted ADRs, the chunk, predecessor receipts,
   dependency manifest, test catalogue, and its canonical implementer prompt.
2. Confirm a clean approved source snapshot and identify unrelated user work.
   Resolve dependency availability/provenance and baseline check limitations.
3. Implement only that chunk and approved supporting changes. A shared Academy,
   SDK, or Harness change needs its own reviewed revision and regression evidence;
   preserve active work and do not move another project's main branch casually.
4. Run exact checks from the approved command manifest. Use deterministic local
   fixtures and literal external contracts, then the appropriate native tests.
   Never call hosted application endpoints by accident.
5. Record commands, environments, inputs, results, failures, hashes, limitations,
   and rollback rehearsal. Save raw sensitive evidence privately; commit redacted
   summaries with references/hashes, not credentials or customer bodies.

# 4. Managed HTTP enters native configuration authority

Date: 2026-10-16. Status: selected following owner candidate selection; independent G01 verdict
and implementation readiness are tracked in planning/status.md. Implements D014,D016 and C14/C15 requirements.

V1's workbench has real request-document and transport depth. Its redactions-based
redirect guard is not explicit tenant-credential classification, Live mode lacks
application destination binding, and its post-401 retry can resend a mutation.
The stricter v2 review/no-replay policy must be enforced below every Send path.

Keep RequestDocument reconciliation separate. Native execution admission captures
a fresh immutable effective request and explicitly distinguishes tenant-managed,
workbench-owned and anonymous credentials. Known managed reads need capability/
destination admission. Known mutations need exact Configuration review. Unknown
managed methods/paths are denied, even if presented as a read or generic draft.
Ordinary workbench-owned/anonymous HTTP remains supported.

Replace the editable SCM collection-ID credential gate with native-owned
capability registration. Imported IDs/references cannot authorize tenant secret
resolution. An edited token_url/request URL is admitted against the explicit
credential destination before secrets are obtained; an ID change never creates
a capability. Preserve operator-reviewed endpoint configuration separately.

Bind review to expanded URL/method/headers/body and file hashes, variables,
cookies, credential/context/destination and resource classification. Recheck
before dispatch; changed input/context/files require fresh review. Rust constructs
the actual request; renderer fields cannot mark it preapproved.

Managed redirects are disabled initially: a 3xx is shown, and following it is a
new prepared/admitted request. Generic redirects preserve bounded cookie/credential
origin policy. No automatic workbench resend follows HTTP401, refresh, reconnect,
lost response, import or history replay. Refresh can precede a new explicit Send.

The built-in catalogue has 193 request specifications, 81 with mutation methods;
this is metadata parity, not a claim of dedicated/live-qualified product support.
Tests cover imported/edited requests, unknown managed endpoints, direct IPC bypass,
ambiguous paths/auth headers, same/cross-origin redirects, stale cookie/file/
variable/context bindings, double Apply and post-401/lost-response no resend.
